kernel.governing_law: What is past and intimate was once sufficient in its simplicity; time divides the living from that sufficiency — the beloved's former state (small, plain, near) is separated from the present by loss, commerce, cold, and growth.
kernel.mutated_relation: The former and the present constitute each other — the plain thing and the elaborate thing are one gesture; the small awkward body and the grown body are simultaneous; the cold that slows the heart is the heart's own warm action of gathering itself.

artifacts.enantiomorph:
*Sappho 98a*

When she was young,
my mouth opened,
the hands used to bind wet roots
with river-silt,

or press caught light
through folds of morning-warm,
and that was a single weight.

Now they wear thick patience
drawn from the same ground.

*Sappho 42*

when winter cold
    builds over the heart, wing
beats close,
    then pressure

*Sappho 49*

long ago I knew you, Atthis,
when you were unfinished clay,
and you were so
dense and
exact.

independent.recovered_law: In Text A, adornment and memory involve decorative, external, and aesthetic elements (purple bands, fresh flowers, gaudy things from Sardis, love, smallness/awkwardness). In Text B, these are replaced by material, tactile, earth-bound substances and processes (wet roots, river-silt, caught light, thick patience drawn from the ground, unfinished clay, density/exactness), transforming the relation from surface decoration to deep material substance.
independent.law_match_note: The recovered claim identifies a real structural change — from surface/decorative to deep/material substance — which partially overlaps the declared mutual constitution of opposites (plain/elaborate, former/present) but frames it as a replacement rather than a simultaneous co-constitution, naming a different relational transformation.
independent.terminal_note: The final fragment (Sappho 49) sustains the shift from aesthetic/decorative/sentimental relation to material/substantive relation ('unfinished clay,' 'dense and exact').
